title: Differential torsion defect of a section over a trait
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction field $K$ and residue field $k$, and choose a strict henselization $A=R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ with residue field $k^{\mathrm{sep}}$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Let $X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a flat locally finite type scheme with smooth generic fibre [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For any $R$-morphism $a:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ set $V_a=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,a^*\Omega^1_{X/R})$ [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf, def-pc-module-pullback]. The module $V_a$ is finitely generated over the discrete valuation ring $A$; its torsion submodule $\{v:\exists\,0\ne t\in A,\ tv=0\}$ has finite length [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Writing $\delta_X(a)$ for that length, one has $\delta_X(a)=0$ if and only if $X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth at the image of the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. These assertions need no quasi-compactness of $X$ and no uniform bound as $a$ varies.

source.place: BLR 3.3 opening paragraph and Lemma 1, printed p.65 (PDF page 71); local finite type refinement by restriction to an affine neighbourhood of the section. Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf.

proof.text: Write $x=a(s_A)$ and $z=a(\eta_A)$ for the images of the closed and generic points. A DVR is a PID, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal]. Let $\Omega$ be an algebraic closure of $k^{\mathrm{sep}}$ and $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ the closed geometric point; the separable algebraic closure of $k$ in $\Omega$ is $k^{\mathrm{sep}}$. By [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison] with $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $D=R$ and $i$ the identity, the geometric strict local ring $\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{\operatorname{Spec}R,\bar x}$ is $R$-isomorphic to a strict henselization of $R$ relative to $k^{\mathrm{sep}}$, compatibly with the residue identifications; two such universal colimit vertices are $R$-isomorphic, so it is $R$-isomorphic to the chosen $A$. Apply [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dvr] to $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$ at $\bar x$: its local ring there is $R$, so $R\to A$ is flat, local and injective, and $A$ is a DVR. Injectivity means the zero ideal of $A$ contracts to the zero ideal of $R$, so $z$ lies in the generic fibre $X_K$. Put $F=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ and $l=k^{\mathrm{sep}}$. Choose an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $x$ on which $B$ is a finite-type $R$-algebra. The preimage $a^{-1}U$ is an open of the local spectrum $\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing its closed point; every prime generalizes that point, so this preimage is the whole spectrum. Thus the entire section factors through $U$. In particular no finite cover of $X$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0AP3 (lemma-henselization-dvr); etale-cohomology.tex Tag 04HX (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring); BLR 3.3 opening paragraph, local affine reduction

proof.text: Let $M=\Gamma(U,\Omega^1_{X/R})=\Omega_{B/R}$. By [lem-trf-relative-differential-sheaf-base-change], relative differentials are quasi-coherent and finite type for a locally finite type morphism, with the indicated affine and base-change identifications. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections], $V_a\cong M\otimes_B A$. Explicitly, if $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ generate $B$ as an $R$-algebra, then $db_1,\ldots,db_n$ generate $M$: the Leibniz rule expands the differential of every polynomial in the $b_i$. Consequently the elements $db_i\otimes1$ generate $V_a$ over $A$. The same affine formula identifies $V_a\otimes_A F$ and $V_a\otimes_A l$ with the differential fibres at the two points, after extension of their residue fields to $F$ and $l$, respectively.

Choose a surjection $A^n\twoheadrightarrow V_a$ and put $N$ equal to its kernel. Apply [lem-sfb-pid-submodule-smith-bases] with ambient module $A^n$ and $O=A^n$. It gives a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ of $A^n$ and a basis $v_1,\ldots,v_r$ of $N$, $r\le n$, with $v_i=c_i e_i$. Each $c_i$ is nonzero, since $v_i$ is a basis vector. The coordinate map sends the class of $\sum u_i e_i$ to $( (u_i\bmod c_i)_{i\le r},(u_i)_{i>r})$ and has kernel exactly $N$. It therefore identifies $V_a$ with $A^{n-r}\oplus\bigoplus_{i=1}^r A/(c_i)$. An element of this direct sum is torsion precisely when its free coordinates vanish: nonzero scalars act injectively on $A$, while $\prod c_i$ kills all cyclic coordinates. Hence the torsion submodule $T$ is the displayed finite sum of cyclic quotients.

By [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one], $\dim A=1$; $A$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal]. Each nonzero $c_i$ is a nonzerodivisor, so [lem-weil-pbc-dim-le-one-principal-quotient-finite-length] gives finite length of $A/(c_i)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] successively to the split exact sequences for a finite direct sum. It follows that $T$ has finite length and $\delta_X(a)$ is a finite nonnegative integer. The definition [def-weil-pbc-module-length] gives length zero exactly for the zero module: a nonzero module has the strict chain $0\subsetneq T$. Thus $\delta_X(a)=0$ exactly when all cyclic summands in Step 3 vanish, equivalently when $V_a$ is free. Conversely a free module has no torsion because $A$ is a domain. This also includes $r=0$, $n=0$ and unit coefficients $c_i$.

If $X/R$ is smooth at $x$, [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-differentials-free-rank-fibre-dimension] gives an affine neighbourhood $W$ of $x$ on which its relative differential module is free of finite rank. As in Step 1, $a$ factors through $W$. The affine pullback formula [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] makes $V_a$ a free $A$-module. Its torsion is therefore zero, and Step 4 gives $\delta_X(a)=0$. Smoothness at a point means smoothness on an open neighbourhood, so the cited smooth-morphism assertion applies to that neighbourhood.

Assume $\delta_X(a)=0$, so Step 4 writes $V_a\cong A^d$ for some $d\ge0$. The point $z$ lies in $X_K$ by Step 1, and $X_K$ is smooth there by hypothesis. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-dimension-differentials], its differential fibre has dimension $\dim_z X_K$ over $\kappa(z)$. The affine base-change identification of Step 2 shows that its extension to $F$ is $V_a\otimes_A F\cong F^d$. A basis over $\kappa(z)$ remains a basis after extension to $F$, so $d=\dim_z X_K$. On the special fibre, the same identification gives $(M\otimes_B\kappa(x))\otimes_{\kappa(x)}l\cong V_a\otimes_A l\cong l^d$. Again a field extension preserves the size of a finite basis, so $\dim_{\kappa(x)}(M\otimes_B\kappa(x))=d$. No assumption that $x$ or $z$ has the base field as residue field is used.

source.place: BLR 3.3 opening paragraph and Lemma 1; Tag 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field), implication (1) to (3)

proof.text: Let $e=\dim_x X_k$, which is a finite nonnegative integer since $X_k$ is locally of finite type over a field. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-fibre-dimension-open], the subset where local fibre dimension is at most $e$ is open and contains $x$. The point $z$ generalizes $x$ because $\eta_A$ generalizes $s_A$ and $a$ is continuous. Hence this open contains $z$ as well. Its fibre there is the generic fibre, so $d=\dim_z X_K\le e$. This is precisely the relative-dimension specialization comparison used in BLR; the lemma requires only local finite type, with no properness or quasi-compactness.

source.place: Tag 02FZ (lemma-openness-bounded-dimension-fibres), reference EGA IV 13.1.3; BLR 3.3 Lemma 1 converse

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ represent $x$. The local module $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is finite, and its residue vector space has dimension $d$ by Step 6. Lift a basis of that vector space to $M_{\mathfrak q}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] these $d$ lifts generate $M_{\mathfrak q}$, hence the differential stalk at $x$. The base $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is locally Noetherian, so [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] makes $X/R$ locally of finite presentation. The stalk map is flat by the assumed flatness of $X/R$. Since $d\le e=\dim_xX_k$, [lem-trf-smooth-at-point-differential-criterion] now gives smoothness at $x$. All hypotheses of this criterion have thus been supplied: local finite presentation, local flatness, and the number of differential generators.

source.place: Tag 01V9 (lemma-smooth-at-point), equivalence (1) and (3); Algebra 00DV (lemma-NAK); BLR 3.3 Lemma 1 converse

proof.text: The constructions and comparisons above concern one fixed section and an affine neighbourhood of its closed image. Step 1 shows that this neighbourhood contains the whole section. Thus none of the conclusions uses quasi-compactness of $X$, and the finite integer $\delta_X(a)$ is established separately for each $a$, without taking a supremum over sections or assuming a uniform bound.
